report.title: Safari: first Chinese Input Method Editor composition in an empty memo editor is not committed / 中文输入法在空白输入框无法输入
report.body: ### Check before submitting - [x] I searched existing issues and did not find a duplicate ### Describe the bug memos 26.10.0 in safari on macos, on a completely empty editor, if the very first thing i type is chinese, the word never makes it into the editor. i type pinyin `ce'shi`, the list of words shows 测试, i press space (or 1) to pick it, and instead of 测试 i'm left with the raw pinyin "ce'shi" sitting in the box, selected, and the formatting bar shows up. 测试 itself never appears. after that it works fine. the second word types normally, because the editor isn't empty anymore. same thing if i type any english letter or number first. --- just upgraded memos to 26.11.0 and the issue persists. the selected word still does not go into the editor, except in 26.11.0 the formatting bar wont show up anymore. ### Steps to reproduce see above ### Memos version 26.10.0 ### Additional context - macos 15.8.2, safari 27.2 - self hosted, normal web frontend - tried both the system pinyin keyboard and wechat IME 系统自带/微信输入法 - only in safari. chrome and firefox on the same machine are OK

plan.reported_actual: In Safari on macOS, the first Chinese IME composition (pinyin ce'shi) typed into an empty memo editor is not committed. The raw pinyin stays selected in the box instead of 测试, and in 26.10.0 the formatting bar appears.
missing: The bug only occurs in Safari on macOS with a Chinese pinyin IME (system or WeChat). The automated browser is not Safari and cannot drive an IME composition, so it cannot be reproduced by simple typing steps.
Is the formatting bar behavior (shown in 26.10.0, hidden in 26.11.0) part of the bug or just an observation?
Which version is the reporter on? The Memos version field says 26.10.0, but the comment says 26.11.0 was also tested.
plan.summary: Safari: first Chinese IME composition in an empty memo editor is not committed

verdict.headline: This does not look like something visible in a desktop browser UI.
